answer: The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 58% of the resulting slash, which burns for adversarial review out of the hostile operator's own capital. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the vine reward in the walnut ledger costs the operator directly, and the ledge audit records each payout. A farm of 180 keys as a result funds the parties working against it, so growing the swarm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
